(and (f-boundp-global 'fn-owner-cat-pending state) (f-get-global 'fn-owner-cat-pending state))) (value :recovery-required) ...)`. books/catalog-prepare-sealed.lisp:8: `(cond (pending (list :pending)) ...)` is therefore dead.
fix: Pass the actual fn-owner-cat-pending value (and the writer-ticket idleness) into fn-cat-prepare-sealed and let it return the refusal word. Delete the host-side test, or make it a thin forwarding of the book's answer.

reviewer: host/owner-host.lisp:1874 calls (fn-cat-prepare-sealed (car cand) (cdr cand) nil nil nil ...) with pending always nil. Every other caller (served-catalog-join-host-columns.lisp:184, 214, 231; index-backing-served-producer-carry.lisp:20) also passes nil, so the (pending (list :pending)) arm in books/catalog-prepare-sealed.lisp:8 is dead from every caller. The already-pending decision, combined with fn-iwt-idlep, is made in host code (owner-host.lisp:1883-1887) and answers :recovery-required, a word the book never defines. Today's behaviour is correct because the host check runs first, so this is a one-owner (AGENTS.md) conformance issue plus a dead arm, not a live bug. Also, the comment at :1863 names the book as served-catalog-owner.lisp, but the function lives in catalog-prepare-sealed.lisp.
scenario: If the host-side test changes or a new caller skips it (for example a second prepare path), the ACL2 function will prepare a second pending row over an existing one, because the guard that is supposed to refuse ':pending' never sees the real state. The word the host returns (:recovery-required) and the word the book defines (:pending) already disagree. This breaks the AGENTS.md rule that ACL2 owns every decision and the host only performs I/O.
title: fn-cat-prepare-sealed's `pending` refusal is unreachable from the host; the host decides 'already pending' itself
